clue.text: Like Olympians, very arrogant

definitions.meaning: the gods of Mount Olympus are lofty and all-powerful, seated far above mortals
haughtily overbearing, giving oneself airs of superiority

explanation.surface: Elite athletes at the Games are described as insufferably conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympians' suggests athletes at the Olympic Games, but here it means the Greek gods on Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for overbearing pride, literally the lofty and powerful position of gods.

clue.text: Gallantry of male officer protecting French king

indicators.note: protecting means the officer pieces are wrapped around the king, guarding him on each side

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major, a military officer
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A soldier shows bravery in guarding a French monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is a synonym for bravery, especially courage shown in battle.

clue.text: Where we may club together to play by the sea

definitions.text: Where we may club together to play by the sea

parts.words: Where we may club together to play by the sea
parts.note: reads like a seaside spot where people pool money or join a society, but the club is a golfer's club swung on a coastal course

explanation.surface: A seaside venue where friends pool resources to have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club together' means to share costs, but here it is swinging golf clubs; links courses lie on sandy coastal land, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside course of sandy dunes is the classic setting for the game played with clubs.

clue.text: Muslim prince became erratic, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ruler in the Islamic world started behaving unpredictably.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, also spelt emir, is a title for a ruler or prince in Muslim countries.

clue.text: A sound indicator of one's calling

definitions.text: A sound indicator of one's calling

parts.words: A sound indicator of one's calling
parts.note: reads like a reliable sign of someone's vocation, but it is a device that rings to announce a visitor has called at the house

explanation.surface: A dependable sign of what someone's vocation is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'reliable' and 'calling' like 'profession'; in fact the indicator makes a sound and the calling is a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A chime at the front entrance signals that a visitor has arrived.

clue.text: It's natural to see British soldiers going into pub

indicators.note: going into means the British soldiers enter the pub, placed inside its letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: It is only to be expected that British troops head into a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn qualities are innate, present from birth rather than learned.

clue.text: Main deck for the top band?

parts.note: head as an adjective means main or chief, as in head office
to deck is to adorn or dress up

explanation.surface: The principal floor of a ship is reserved for the best musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main deck' suggests a ship and 'top band' a leading group of musicians; the band is something worn on the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative covering worn on the head can be a band of ornament, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Over there, outside this country, where prospects were good

indicators.note: outside means the word for over there sits around the country, enclosing it

parts.note: yon is an old word for over there, as in yonder
UK, the United Kingdom, is this country for a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Somewhere abroad, the opportunities looked promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospects' looks like career chances but means gold prospecting: the Klondike gold rush was in the Yukon territory of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian territory saw the Klondike gold rush, when miners searched there for gold.

clue.text: Popular minister to have in mind

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A well-liked clergyman wishes to plan something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun for a clergyman, but it is the verb meaning to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan or purpose something is to keep it in your thoughts as an aim.

clue.text: Backward over accepting fiction as outstanding work

indicators.note: accepting means the reversed word takes the fiction inside it
backward means the word over is read in reverse order

parts.note: the word is taken as written before being turned round
a lie is a fiction, an untruth

explanation.surface: A reluctant critic warms to a novel as a superb piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' makes REVO and 'accepting' takes in the fiction. 'Outstanding' is literal here: relievo is relief sculpture, whose figures stand out from the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief sculpture is carving in which figures project from the background surface.

clue.text: Lamb partly hidden by mountain ferns

indicators.note: hidden by means the cut of lamb is enclosed within the mountain's letters

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a rack is one part of a lamb, a joint of ribs

explanation.surface: A sheep is half concealed among the vegetation on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' suggests a hidden run in 'Lamb', but a rack is a cut of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large coarse fern growing densely on hillsides; the mass noun covers many plants.

clue.text: Terrible ride with new driver, one frequently unemployed

indicators.note: terrible means the letters are put in an awful, jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver

explanation.surface: A dreadful car journey with a learner at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer who avoids work is often without a job.

clue.text: Run into musicians at an Anglican church social event

indicators.note: into means the run goes inside the word for musicians

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Bumping into a band at a parish get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: A barn dance is an informal country dance, often held in a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A country dance gathering is a lively social occasion.

clue.text: Servant, though advanced in years, performing several functions

parts.note: a man is a manservant
if can mean though, as in 'pleasant, if dull'
old means advanced in years

explanation.surface: An elderly retainer still carries out a variety of duties.
explanation.walkthrough: A manifold in an engine is a pipe with several outlets, so the word suits many functions.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and varied, having numerous forms or uses.

clue.text: African country scores without strictly following convention

indicators.note: without means outside, so the scores wrap around the country

parts.note: two scores, each twenty, make forty
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A team from Africa scores freely without regard to the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Formality is rigid observance of rules and etiquette; the clue gives the behaviour rather than the noun's name.

clue.text: Bloody conflict confined within desert

indicators.note: confined within means the conflict is held inside the word for bloody

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A violent battle restricted to an arid wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand dunes but is the noun from 'just deserts', what one deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert, as in just deserts, is what one has earned, a due recompense.

clue.text: One of the well-protected beginners Kipling wrote about

definitions.text: One of the well-protected beginners Kipling wrote about

parts.words: One of the well-protected beginners Kipling wrote about
parts.note: refers to a Just So Story telling how a pair of creatures came to have their tough armoured shells

explanation.surface: A carefully sheltered novice in one of Kipling's tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories include 'The Beginning of the Armadilloes', explaining how they got their armour.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured mammal is the subject of a Kipling story about its origin.

clue.text: Honour painter, one who transformed the house

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour
a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A decorated painter turned out to be a home renovator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The house' is the House of Commons: the 19th-century Chartist movement demanded electoral reform, most of it later enacted.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartists campaigned for parliamentary reform, such as votes for all men and secret ballots, changing who sits in the Commons.

clue.text: Wretchedness of quarters in muddy environment

indicators.note: environment means the muddy word surrounds the quarters, as their setting

parts.note: miry means muddy, like a mire
S and E are two compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Unhappiness from living in squalid lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests lodgings, but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery and wretchedness are synonyms for deep unhappiness.

clue.text: Title of French woman architect in Maine

indicators.note: in means the architect is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine
Robert Adam was a famous Scottish architect

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's form of address while designing buildings in Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French courtesy title for a married woman, like Mrs.

clue.text: He's accommodated in Civil Service employee's castle, perhaps

indicators.note: accommodated in means the he's letters are housed within the service abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
a man is an employee or worker

explanation.surface: A man lodges in the stately home of a government worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castle' suggests a building but is the chess piece also called a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle, or rook, is one of the pieces used in chess, given as an example.

clue.text: Material that makes Indian bread bitter

parts.note: nan, or naan, is an Indian flatbread
keen can mean bitter, as in a keen, biting wind

explanation.surface: A fabric that gives Indian flatbread a sour taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a type of cotton fabric, so it is an example of material.

clue.text: Mike's employed here with boss I love

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob
O is zero, love in tennis

explanation.surface: A man called Mike works here alongside his manager, whom he adores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a name, but is a microphone. 'Boss' is not an employer but a raised ornament or knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Microphones are used in a recording or broadcasting room.

clue.text: He takes away rubbish carried from back to front

indicators.note: from back to front means both words together are read in reverse

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense
carted means carried

explanation.surface: A dustman removes garbage, lugging it through the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From back to front' turns ROTCARTED round to give the answer. A detractor takes away from someone's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who disparages others diminishes their good name, taking from it.

clue.text: Invigorating do for musicians

definitions.meaning: in ... sol-fa, doh is the keynote of the scale

explanation.surface: A lively party held for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party but is the first note of the scale, the keynote.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means restorative; in music it names the keynote, called do in sol-fa.

clue.text: If too close, a dangerously silly position of fellow on motorway

definitions.text: If too close, a dangerously silly position

indicators.note: on means the fellow comes after the motorway, following it

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A driver warns that stopping too close on the motorway is foolhardy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielder at mid-on placed very near the batsman is called silly mid-on, an exposed spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly is the cricket term for fielding positions very near the batsman, risky ones.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker's place in West

definitions.note: possessive: the cabinet-maker's wood, a material belonging to the furniture maker

indicators.note: in means the place abbreviation sits inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was an American actress

explanation.surface: A furniture maker sets up shop in the western part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction but is the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood prized by furniture craftsmen for cabinets.

clue.text: People generally object to receiving a new king

indicators.note: receiving means the word for object takes in the other letters

parts.note: to mind is to object
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: The public protests at being given a new monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Mankind means the human race, humanity as a whole.

clue.text: Sort of buying that is stopped by terrible slump

indicators.note: stopped by means the scrambled letters plug the gap inside the abbreviation

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: terrible means the word slump is put into disorder

explanation.surface: Spontaneous shopping comes to a halt in a dire recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' gives MPULS, plugged into the gap by 'stopped by'. 'Sort of buying' points to the phrase impulse buying, purchases made on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulse buying is purchasing on a sudden whim without planning.

clue.text: Have unrealistic aspiration, in theory -— conform otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are arranged in a different way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreamer's ambitions work in principle, but life demands compliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means wanting something impossible to get, like grasping at the sky.
